items.title: Reflection AI unveils Beam, a 501B-parameter open-weight MoE; Apache 2.0 weights promised later in October
items.summary: Nvidia-backed Reflection debuted its first model, Beam, on Oct 5: a 501B-total, 23B-active MoE pretrained on 23.8T tokens with a 1M-token context. Reflection says it is competitive with Z.ai's GLM-5.2 on coding and agentic tasks while using 3-4x less inference compute. Early access is by waitlist; weights, a technical report and a model card are due under Apache 2.0 later in October. TechCrunch notes the claims are unverified, and Beam trails Kimi K3 on Terminal-Bench and DeepSWE.
items.why_it_matters: It is the first serious US-built open-weight challenger to the Chinese models that dominate open rankings. The weights have not shipped, so independent testing is still pending.

items.summary: On Oct 5 Huawei and Qualcomm announced a multi-year cross-licence across 5G, computing, AI and networking. Qualcomm will also buy selected Huawei US patents in compute, AI and networking. Reports say Qualcomm becomes the net payer for the first time in the firms' 25-year licensing history, and this is the first Huawei-Qualcomm deal to cover 5G. The deal needs regulatory approval; financial terms and timing were not disclosed.

items.title: NYC Council grills OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta on AI risk as ex-Anthropic researcher Coxon testifies
items.summary: All 51 NYC Council members questioned policy executives from Anthropic (Logan Graham), OpenAI (Morgan Dwyer), Google (Alice Friend) and Meta (Shane Cahill) under oath on Oct 5. Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon told the panel humanity is more likely than not to lose control of AI. Speaker Julie Menin called answers on legal liability 'troubling at best'. The firms reportedly agreed to appear only after subpoena threats. Menin's bill would bar selling or deploying an AI model in NYC unless an outside validator has reviewed it and a person can shut it down.
items.why_it_matters: A US city is moving toward binding frontier-AI safeguards while federal policy stays light-touch, adding to the state and local patchwork the labs face.
key_numbers: Bill: outside validator plus human shutdown

items.title: Pentagon tells BBC it has ceased using Anthropic products, though sources say Claude was still used via Maven last week
items.summary: A Defense Department official told the BBC on Oct 5 that the Pentagon 'has ceased the use of Anthropic products'. This follows Hegseth's February supply-chain-risk designation and a six-month phaseout. BBC sources said Claude was still used as recently as last week, including in operations against Iran, through Palantir's Maven Smart System.
items.why_it_matters: It marks the formal end of the largest government deployment of a frontier lab's model after a dispute over safeguards, and shows how hard it is to extract an embedded model from classified workflows.

items.title: Goldman: US data-center growth intact despite local opposition; 2026 forecast raised to 64 GW, 2027 trimmed to 90 GW
items.summary: Goldman Sachs raised its end-2026 US data-center capacity forecast by 5 GW to 64 GW and cut end-2027 by 5 GW to 90 GW. It expects US data-center power demand to grow 38% (12 GW) in 2026 and 38% (17 GW) in 2027. Its view is that moratoria and community pushback have had limited near-term impact because developers shift to friendlier jurisdictions. A June Reuters/Ipsos poll found only 14% would support a local AI data center.
items.why_it_matters: Wall Street reads the backlash as moving where AI capacity gets built rather than how much, with some 2027 build pulled into 2026.

items.title: Samsung set for first 100-trillion-won quarter: Q3 operating profit seen near 107-108T won on memory boom
items.summary: Ahead of Samsung's preliminary Q3 release, expected this week, consensus operating profit is about 106.9T won (FnGuide, Oct 2) to 108.1T won, roughly ninefold year on year. items.title: China reportedly spent $13B+ stockpiling ASML immersion DUV tools in 2024-25, sparking US calls for a full export ban
items.summary: TrendForce reports Chinese fabs spent over $13B on about 90 ASML NXT:1980i machines in 2024 and 89 in 2025. A separate report puts Chinese-owned fabs at an estimated 343 immersion DUV systems by early 2026, around 270 of them NXT:1980i, which can be adapted for 7nm-class chips. China was 41% of ASML's system sales in 2024 and 33% in 2025. SCMP says the stockpile is driving US calls for a complete export ban on the tools.
items.why_it_matters: It shows how much licensed DUV supply has fed China's advanced-chip push and adds pressure on Washington and The Hague to tighten approvals.
key_numbers: China 41% of ASML system sales 2024, 33% in 2025

items.title: DeepSeek Harness holiday update adds experimental Claude Code Mods compatibility layer
items.original_title: DeepSeek国庆假期更新Harness，加入实验性Claude Code Mods兼容层
items.summary: DeepSeek's agent framework Harness shipped alpha v0.2.1-alpha.1 on Oct 3, strengthening plugin and cross-platform support and adding an experimental layer that can run some of Anthropic's Claude Code Mods extensions. Team member Cui Tianyi, who wrote the layer, says it tests whether Mods capabilities are a subset of Harness's 'everything is a plugin' architecture. It cannot yet run all Mods, but he says full support is technically feasible.
items.why_it_matters: A Chinese lab is making its agent harness interoperable with a leading US coding agent's extension ecosystem, which could ease developer migration between the stacks.

items.title: Crunchbase: Q3 venture hit $159B with a record 27 billion-dollar rounds; AI took 64%
items.summary: Crunchbase reports global venture funding of $159B in Q3 2026 across close to 6,000 startups, down 25% from Q2 but up 53% year on year. A record 27 companies raised $1B+ rounds, about a third of all dollars. AI-driven startups raised $102B (64%). Databricks and Safe Superintelligence led with $5B each. Funding for Q1-Q3 totals $679B, the highest first nine months on record.
items.why_it_matters: Capital is concentrating in a handful of giant AI and compute rounds even as total quarterly funding cooled from Q2's peak.

items.title: TSMC US shares hit record as Musk-confirmed Terafab talks reshape the Oct 15 earnings preview
items.summary: TSMC's US-listed shares reached fresh records near $477-480 on Oct 5, closing up about 3%, after Musk confirmed early talks with TSMC on the Texas Terafab. TrendForce's preview says the structure could range from TSMC owning and operating the fab with Terafab/SpaceX taking equity or wafer commitments, to Musk's side holding a majority with TSMC supplying process technology. TSMC reports Q3 results on Oct 15.
items.why_it_matters: A Musk-linked US foundry deal would depart from TSMC's usual operating model and tie its returns to the counterparties' execution.
